title: Collection of Rosicrucian and Alchemical Texts (PH255)
shelf_note: An 18th-century Latin alchemical manuscript about the antimony regulus, Mercurius philosophorum, purification with Mars and gold, citing Philaletha. It belongs in a Rosicrucian/alchemical collection.
structure_note: The packet has no structure counts, and none of the three pages carries a translation, so this record is OCR-only on the sampled pages. All three images are leaves of the same bound manuscript in the same hand, and none shows a splice. Each frame catches a strip of the facing leaf at the right edge. The OCR says it ignores that strip on two pages and does not read it on the third.

ocr_errors.problem: The OCR expands two alchemical signs into words. It flags both as unclear, and the heading 'Mercurii mediante Arsenico' makes the reading plausible, but it is a guess and not a reading.
Expanding the salt sign to 'Sale' is reasonable. The page warning discloses that signs are expanded.

other.note: The page has no translation. The packet's translation field is null, so a reader gets Latin only.

ocr_errors.ocr: 5 aut 6 lot ⊖i et paucam quantitatem ⊖ fusi
ocr_errors.image: 5 aut 6 lot Øi (a circle with an oblique stroke) … quantitate ⊖ fusi (a circle with a horizontal bar)
ocr_errors.problem: Two different signs on the leaf both become ⊖, so the two ingredients of the recipe merge into one. The same happens again in 'lot ⊖i … ⊖is quantitate' and 'augmentationem ⊖i'.

ocr_errors.image: necdum ☿rialia (a mercury sign plus '-rialia', i.e. mercurialia)
ocr_errors.problem: 'Mercurialia' is read as 'corporalia', which changes the sense of the explanation. The OCR flags it as unclear.

ocr_errors.image: ad augmentationem Øi et [a small sign, possibly ☉o] fixationemque ☿ri
ocr_errors.problem: The OCR seems to drop a sign after 'et', and it reads the mercury sign as ♀ (flagged unclear). I read this at low confidence.
The signs in the list of three principles are uncertain or confused. The OCR flags one of them.

other.note: The page has no translation. The packet's translation field is null.

ocr_errors.ocr: quamvis autem Reguli nomine optime purificatus ♁ purissimi coagulati typum
ocr_errors.image: quamvis autem Regl[us] nr[oste]r optime purificatus ☿ii purissimi coagulati typum
ocr_errors.problem: The abbreviation 'Regulus noster' is read as 'Reguli nomine', and the mercury sign ('☿ii') becomes ♁. The image says our Regulus bears the type of the purest coagulated mercury; the OCR makes the 'purified antimony' the subject.
At this resolution the sign looks like the antimony sign (a circle with a cross above), not Mars, so the ingredient in the dose may be wrong. Low confidence.

ocr_errors.image: Purgatio ♁ii cum [a sign shaped like the sulphur/Jupiter glyph]ro
ocr_errors.problem: The sign is uncertain. It may not be Mars.

other.note: The page has no translation. The packet's translation field is null.
The later pencil annotation ('V. p. sequ: 7. ubi d. … nomin:') is tagged as <margin> and disclosed in <meta> as a later hand. That is handled correctly and is not a defect.

book_verdict: The transcription of this Latin alchemical manuscript is faithful, with the uncertain words flagged. Its weak point is the alchemical signs: distinct signs are merged or swapped, and that changes which ingredient a step or dose names. The sampled pages have no English translation.
